ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, there is a cylinder with an inner radius of 2r and a length of L. Small holes are opened at the centers $O^{\prime}$ and $O$ of the left and right end faces, respectively. A coordinate system is established with $O$ as the origin, and the direction from $O^{\prime}$ to $O$ as the positive x-axis direction. There is a uniform magnetic field in the region $x \le 0$ inside the cylinder, with a magnetic induction magnitude of B, and the direction is along the positive x-axis. There is a uniform electric field in the region $x \ge 0$ outside the cylinder, with an electric field strength magnitude of E, and the direction is along the positive y-axis. An electron gun at $O^{\prime}$ emits electrons in multiple directions into the cylinder. The initial velocities of the electrons are all within the $xOy$ plane, and the magnitude of the velocity component in the positive x-axis direction is $v_{0}$. Given that the mass of the electron is $m$ and the charge is $e$, assume that the electrons do not collide with the cylinder walls, and neglect the interactions between electrons and the gravity of the electrons.

1. If all electrons can pass through $O$ and enter the electric field, determine the minimum value of the magnetic induction B.
2. Using the minimum magnetic induction magnitude B found in (1), if the maximum angle between the velocity direction of the electrons entering the magnetic field and the positive x-axis is $\theta$, calculate the absolute value of $\tan \theta$.
3. Using the minimum magnetic induction magnitude B found in (1), calculate the maximum displacement of the electrons along the positive y-axis when they move in the electric field.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$B_{\text{min}} = \frac{2\pi m v_{0}}{e L}$
$\tan \theta = \frac{2\pi r}{L}$
$y_{\mathrm{{m}}}= \frac{2\pi^{2}r^{2}v_{0}^{2}m}{E e L^{2}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a horizontally placed cylindrical region; the cylinder axis is along the horizontal x direction, pointing from the small hole O′ at the center of the left end face to the small hole O at the center of the right end face; O is the coordinate origin, the x axis is to the right, the y axis is upward, and the z axis is drawn obliquely. The inner radius of the cylinder is marked as 2r, and the length is marked as L. Inside the cylinder there are multiple magnetic-field arrows pointing to the right, marked as B, indicating that the magnetic field is along the +x direction; outside O at the right end there is an upward electric-field arrow, marked as E, indicating that the electric field is along the +y direction. Reasoning: The electron enters the magnetic field from O′, its initial velocity is in the xOy plane, and the velocity component in the x direction is constantly v0. Since the magnetic field B is along the x direction, the Lorentz force does not change v_x, so the time for the electron to go from O′ to O is T=L/v0. Let the initial transverse velocity be v_y=u, and the initial v_z=0. Take the magnitude of the electron charge as e, and the cyclotron angular velocity as omega=eB/m. The transverse motion satisfies uniform circular motion, and can be written as y(t)=(u/omega)sin(omega t), z(t)=(u/omega)[1-cos(omega t)]. To make electrons with any initial transverse velocity u all be able to pass through the center O when reaching the right end face, it is necessary to have y(T)=0 and z(T)=0, that is, sin(omega T)=0 and cos(omega T)=1; therefore omega T=2πn. The minimum nonzero magnetic induction intensity corresponds to n=1, so (eB/m)(L/v0)=2π, obtaining B_min=2πmv0/(eL). Under this minimum magnetic field, omega=2πv0/L. The maximum distance from the transverse trajectory to the cylinder axis is 2|u|/omega. In the figure the inner radius of the cylinder is 2r; in order not to hit the wall, it is necessary that 2|u|/omega <= 2r, and in the maximum case |u|=r omega. Therefore the maximum incidence angle theta satisfies |tan theta|=|u|/v0=r omega/v0=2πr/L. When the electron enters the electric field from O, because it has just completed one period in the magnetic field, the transverse velocity is still the initial u. The electric field E is along the +y direction, while the force on the electron is along the -y direction, and the magnitude of the acceleration is eE/m. To obtain the maximum displacement in the positive y direction, take the maximum positive transverse velocity when entering the electric field as u_max=r omega=2πrv0/L. When the electron decelerates to zero in the y direction, the displacement is maximum; therefore y_m=u_max^2/[2(eE/m)]=m/(2eE)*(2πrv0/L)^2=2π^2r^2v0^2m/(EeL^2).
